headline: Majors sit above their 200-day lines while the crowd feels greedy and BTC quietly moves onto exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it sets the frame for everything else. Five of the seven majors here, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB, sit above their 200-day averages with golden crosses in place, which is a constructive long-term posture. DOGE and ADA are the outliers, both below their 200-day lines with no golden cross, and both down more than 70% from their 12-month highs (DOGE -70.3%, ADA -77.2%) versus BTC's comparatively modest -37.3%. That is not one market, it is two speeds under the same roof.

Momentum is where the story gets interesting, because it is not confirming the trend so much as resting on it. RSI readings across the board sit in the high 50s (BTC 59.2, ETH 60.8, SOL 57.8, XRP 57.2, BNB 58.2), comfortably shy of overbought, and every single asset shows MACD below its signal line. That is a textbook cooling-off pattern: prices well above long-term trend, momentum indicators pulling back from a hotter reading. It is not bearish by itself, but it is a divergence worth naming, the kind of pause that shows up after a strong month (BTC +22.4%, ETH +29.2%, SOL +37.5% over 30 days) runs into a quieter week (BTC -0.4%, ETH -0.0%, SOL -1.8%). The month says trend, the week says rest.

Positioning adds texture. BTC funding on OKX sits at 0.0046% per 8 hours (5.1% annualized), mild and unremarkable, paired with $2.08B open interest and a long/short ratio of 1.33, tilted long but not stretched. ETH funding is barely positive (1.0% annualized) with a 1.57 long/short skew. SOL and XRP are the standouts: both carry negative funding (-10.0% and -11.1% annualized respectively), meaning shorts are paying longs to hold their position, yet their long/short account ratios read 2.06 and 2.54, heavily long-skewed. That combination, crowded long accounts but negative funding, says the big directional bet is long while cheap to hold against, an unusual split. Liquidations lean lopsided too: BTC saw $1.99M in long liquidations against just $118K in shorts over 2 hours, SOL's longs took $1.19M in liquidations against essentially zero on the short side. Leverage is getting flushed on the long side even as accounts stay net long.

Flows are where the disagreement sharpens. BTC spot ETFs printed a $100.7M outflow on Sep 9, yet the five-session net sits at +$859.2M, with same_direction_days at just 2, so the daily print and the trailing week are pointing in different directions right now. ETH ETFs are cleaner: a small $2.1M inflow on the day matches a $96.9M five-session net. Whale activity over the last 24 hours shows $57.97M in BTC moving onto exchanges (all of it into okex, none of it offset by outflows), and the weekly pattern isn't a straight line either: the week ending Aug 27 saw $1,580M onto exchanges, the week ending Sep 3 flipped to $371M off exchanges, and the week ending Sep 10 reversed again to $491M onto exchanges. That is choppy, not trending. Stablecoin float, meanwhile, sits at $310.4B, up 1.42% over 30 days, a slow, steady build in dry powder that doesn't match the whale chop.

Sentiment sits at 69, labeled Greed, near the top of its 30-day range of 27 to 74. That is a crowd that feels good. The tape underneath it is more ambivalent: cooling momentum, a same-day BTC ETF outflow against a positive five-day trend, and net BTC moving onto exchanges in the last 24 hours even as the broader weekly whale pattern has flipped twice in three weeks. Total market cap fell 3.29% on the day to $2.68T even as BTC itself was roughly flat, a sign the damage was concentrated elsewhere (SPX -10.93%, TRUMP -9.72%, PONS -15.71% among the day's losers, while NEAR, ZEC, and XMR gained).

What to watch: whether BTC funding stays positive while long liquidations keep outpacing shorts, a sign of leveraged longs getting cleared out under a still-long-leaning book; whether the next few ETF sessions confirm the five-day inflow trend or extend the single-day outflow; and whether the weekly whale flow pattern settles in one direction for two consecutive prints rather than alternating as it has since Aug 20.
